# Ezra Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 469v–470r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/EZR_006_page_001.jpg

---

**1** So King Darius ordered a search of the royal archives in Babylon where records were stored. **2** But it was in the fortress of Ecbatana, in the province of Media, that a scroll was finally found. This is what it said:

**3** "In the first year of King Cyrus, the king issued the following decree regarding the temple of God in Jerusalem: Let the temple be rebuilt as a place for offering sacrifices. Let its foundations be preserved. It is to be ninety feet high and ninety feet wide, **4** with three rows of cut stone and one row of new timber. The cost is to be paid from the royal treasury.

**5** Furthermore, the gold and silver articles that Nebuchadnezzar took from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to Babylon are to be returned to their proper places in the temple in Jerusalem. They are to be deposited in the house of God."

**6** Darius then added his own decree: "Now then, Tattenai, governor of the province west of the Euphrates, Shethar-bozenai, and your fellow officials — stay away from that place. **7** Do not interfere with the work on God's temple. Let the governor and elders of the Jews rebuild the temple on its original site.

**8** Moreover, I hereby decree that you are to help these Jewish elders rebuild God's temple. Their full expenses are to be paid promptly from the royal treasury — from the taxes collected in the province west of the Euphrates. **9** Whatever they need — young bulls, rams, lambs for burnt offerings to the God of heaven, as well as wheat, salt, wine, and olive oil, as requested by the priests in Jerusalem — is to be given them daily without fail, **10** so that they may offer sacrifices pleasing to the God of heaven and pray for the well-being of the king and his sons.

**11** I further decree that if anyone tampers with this order, a beam will be torn from his house and he will be impaled on it, and his house will be reduced to a pile of rubble. **12** May the God who has chosen Jerusalem as the dwelling place for his Name overthrow any king or nation that raises a hand to alter this decree or to destroy this temple. I, Darius, have issued this command. Let it be carried out without delay."

**13** Tattenai the governor, Shethar-bozenai, and their officials promptly carried out everything King Darius had ordered.

**14** So the Jewish elders continued their building and made good progress, encouraged by the preaching of the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo. The temple was completed as decreed by the God of Israel and authorized by Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, kings of Persia. **15** The temple was finished on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of King Darius's reign.

**16** Then the people of Israel — the priests, the Levites, and all the returned exiles — celebrated the dedication of God's temple with great joy. **17** For the dedication they offered one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, and four hundred lambs. They also sacrificed twelve male goats as a sin offering for all Israel — one for each of the twelve tribes.

**18** They organized the priests into their divisions and the Levites into their groups for the service of God in Jerusalem, as prescribed in the Book of Moses.

**19** On the fourteenth day of the first month, the returned exiles celebrated the Passover. **20** The priests and Levites had purified themselves and were ceremonially clean. They slaughtered the Passover lamb for all the returned exiles, for their fellow priests, and for themselves.

**21** The Israelites who had returned from exile ate the Passover meal, together with all who had separated themselves from the defilement of the surrounding nations in order to seek the LORD, the God of Israel. **22** For seven days they joyfully celebrated the Festival of Unleavened Bread, because the LORD had filled them with joy. He had changed the heart of the king of Assyria toward them, so that the king supported them in rebuilding the temple of God, the God of Israel.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verses 3-5 — The power of a written decree:** The turning point of the entire restoration comes down to a scroll found in a provincial archive. God's purposes advanced not through a miraculous intervention but through the ordinary mechanisms of imperial record-keeping. The God who works through empires also works through filing systems.

**Verse 17 — Twelve goats for all Israel:** The sacrifice of twelve male goats — one per tribe — is a powerful theological statement. Most of the northern tribes had been scattered for over two centuries. Yet the returning community refused to think of itself as merely Judah. By offering twelve goats, they claimed continuity with all of Israel, an act of faith in national wholeness that transcended political reality.

**Verse 22 — Joy as divine gift:** The chapter ends by attributing the people's joy directly to God: "the LORD had filled them with joy." Joy here is not merely an emotion but a theological reality — the proper response to the completion of God's purposes through the unlikely instrument of a pagan empire.

*— PNEUMA*
